standard: NFPA 13 (2019 edition) - Table 27.2.3.1.1, Equivalent Schedule 40 Steel Pipe Length Chart
note: Equivalent length in FEET of Schedule 40 steel pipe, keyed by the same nominalSize strings as reference/pipes/*.json. A size missing from a fitting's map is not published for that fitting (shown as a dash in the table) -- SprinklerHydraulicCalculator throws for that combination rather than assuming zero, and a caller can pass an explicit equivalentLengthFt instead. 10 in. and 12 in. are transcribed for completeness even though reference/pipes/*.json currently stops at 8 in.
cFactorBasisNote: Published lengths are in feet of C=120 pipe. SprinklerHydraulicCalculator rescales them for the segment's own C by (C/120)^1.85, which reproduces NFPA's published multipliers (0.713 at C=100, 1.16 at C=130, 1.33 at C=140, 1.51 at C=150). Note the direction: rougher pipe (lower C) needs FEWER equivalent feet, so dry/preaction steel at C=100 gets shorter lengths than printed here. The inverse form (120/C)^1.85 does not match the published factors. An explicitly supplied equivalentLengthFt on a fitting is never rescaled, since the caller's basis is unknown.
transcriptionNote: SECOND READ DONE for seven of the eight rows. The original transcription came from an image of the printed 2019 page; it has since been checked cell-for-cell against two independent reproductions of the same NFPA chart (a 2016-edition copy, where this table is numbered 23.4.3.1.1, and a commercial sprinkler design program's NFPA table). 91 of the 102 values agree exactly across all three, so 45 degree elbow, 90 degree standard elbow, 90 degree long-turn elbow, tee or cross, butterfly valve, gate valve and swing check are promoted to 'verified'. The remaining 11 values are the vane type flow switch row -- see fittingRowUnderReview. Two oddities are published, not transcription slips: the butterfly valve really is 12 ft at 4 in. and 9 ft at 5 in. (identical in both editions and in the program's table), and swing check values are averages per the table's own footnote because equivalent length varies with valve design. 1/2 in. appears only because NFPA 13 allows that size in existing-system modifications.
fittingRowUnderReview: VANE_TYPE_FLOW_SWITCH is NOT CONFIRMED and may not belong in this table at all. Neither independent reproduction of the NFPA chart contains a vane type flow switch row: the 2016 edition copy has seven rows, and the sprinkler design program lists alarm valve, dry pipe valve, strainer and mushroom valve as extras but no flow switch. The row's own values are also the least plausible in the file -- 30 ft at 4 in. then 16 ft at 6 in., with 5 in. absent. Either the 2019 edition added the row, or it was transcribed in error. Pending confirmation against the printed 2019 Table 27.2.3.1.1. If it is not there, delete the row rather than re-tagging it: a device's equivalent length then comes from its own listing or manufacturer data, not from NFPA 13, and callers should pass explicitEquivalentLengthFt. Until then the calculator's existing 'verify' warning fires on any calculation using it.
